newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Interior Ministry has approved a police request seeking the arrest of Senator Sukhum Cherdchuen, accused of masterminiding the murder of a doctor. Fearing that the senator may use influence and wealth to flee, the interior minister urges the Senate to approve Sukhum's arrest, adding that there is substantial evidence to take action against him. (THE NATION, (BANGKOK POST)

- The structure of the planned administrative court will be decided next week, said Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh after he apologised in person to the Supreme Court president for listening to the judges' side of the argument too late. The Supreme Court president insisted after the meeting that the new court would reside within the existing court system at the Justice Ministry, and not under the Council of State as Chavalit had earlier said. (THE NATION)

- Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong has hinted that the National Housing Authority (NHA) governor could be removed over controversial land purchases. Snoh has also shrugged off a morale-boosting campaign being carried out by NHA employees for the governor. (THE NATION)

- If ongoing efforts to get the Port Authority of Thailand (PAT) to cancel the monopoly on freight services at Klong Toey port succeed, the Express Transportation Organisation (ETO) will suffer considerably, says ETO President Manop Avuchanon. Private operators have been pressuring the government to cancel the ETO monopoly. A number of haulage operators have been unofficially operating out of Klong Toey port and it is believed they are paying 35 percent of their receipts to ETO for the privilege. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand has been taken aback by the strength of disagreement over its scheme to bail out the ailing property sector. Although the central bank never expected the package to win unanimous support, so far only Bangkok Bank and Siam Commercial Bank have agreed to join the scheme. Other banks have signalled their reluctance to join the scheme. (BANGKOK POST)

- Transport and Communications Minister Suwat Liptapanlop has proposed that Thai Airways International Plc find strategic partners to boost its operations and further privatise its ownership. Suwat says a bigger private sector equity interest in THAI would strengthen the airline's business prospects. (THE NATION)
